table.title: [Stratigraphic Succession of Formations in North and Central China]

rows: Helicadae shells, ostrich eggs, tusks and molars of Elephant.
Widely distributed all over N. China.
Fresh water mollusca as Quadrula and Cuneoposis.
Sanmen Rapids on the Yellow River, Honan; also N. of Ordos.
Hipparion clay. Prob. also the "Deck sandstein" of S. China.
Red and variegated clays with layers of gravels (often conglomeratic).
Hipparion, Rhinoceros, Deer, Antelope, Hyena, etc.; also Suidae, Probascidae, Cynocephalus, etc.
Widely distributed in N. China. The lignite deposits of E. Yunnan containing plant fossils and gastropoda are probably of the same age.
Coal series interbedded with basaltic lavas. The coal is lignitic to subbituminous.
Plant fossils: Osmunda, Sequoia, Glyptostrabus, Populus, Fugus etc.
Fushun and Shihmenchai in S. Manchuria. Also N. Shensi and inner Mongolia.
Yuanchu series in Honan and Kuanchang series in Shantung.
Thick conglomerate interbedded with sandstones, clays and marls.
Planorbis, Physa Euchilus, Eupera and bones of reptiles and mammals.
Widely distributed in N. China from Kansu to Shantung.

table.title: General History of the Tectonic Movements and Igneous Activities

rows: Vertical movements resulted in warping or block faulting. Folding insignificant.
Extrusion of extensive Miocene basalt and possibly also most of the porphyries.
“Horst” or “Graben” are formed in some regions as a result of the vertical displacement. Such movement may still be going on to-day as evidenced by the distribution of the seismic centres.
Intense horizontal movement producing folding, thrusting or shearing.
Intrusion of granite and diabasic sheet, extrusion of lava flow.
The Tsingling range was formed at this period.
Epirogenic movement i.e. the strata are not folded—disconformity.
Orogenic movement all over the country—marked unconformity between the Wutai and the younger formations.
Intrusion of granites, diorites, gabbros, etc. Intense metamorphism
In the Wutai system itself, three epochs of tectonic movements may be distinguished.
Great orogenic movements—marked unconformity between Wutai and Archaean.
